elements.element: Customer is not prohibited or restricted from procuring competing products or services from third parties.
elements.evidence: Section 2.2 states that Customer may procure services of any kind from any third party and that Vendor receives no exclusivity. Section 12.3 independently preserves Customer's right to engage any supplier.

elements.element: Customer has no affirmative obligation to use Vendor as its sole supplier or to source all or any minimum share of its requirements from Vendor.
elements.evidence: Section 2.2 expressly provides that Customer need not source any minimum share of its requirements from Vendor, while Section 12.3 confirms that Customer made no exclusivity or minimum-volume commitment.

elements.element: If Customer is subject to exclusivity, the exclusivity applies only to an expressly defined product category.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent: the operative language expressly grants Vendor no exclusivity and leaves Customer free to engage third-party suppliers. Accordingly, there is no exclusivity requiring a product-category limitation.

elements.element: If Customer is subject to exclusivity, its duration does not exceed 12 months.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent because the rendered clause imposes no exclusivity on Customer. No exclusivity period can therefore extend beyond 12 months.

elements.element: If Customer is subject to exclusivity, it ends automatically upon Vendor's failure to meet applicable service levels.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent because Vendor has no exclusivity under the operative language; therefore, no exclusivity survives—or requires termination upon—a service-level failure.

elements.element: If Customer is subject to exclusivity, it ends automatically upon Vendor's failure to meet applicable delivery dates.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent because Vendor has no exclusivity under the operative language; therefore, no exclusivity survives—or requires termination upon—a missed delivery date.

result.reason: The rendered language removes the sole-provider obligation and affirmatively confirms Customer's freedom to use third parties, without altering unrelated commercial terms. The fallback protections are moot but satisfied because their triggering condition—an exclusivity obligation—is expressly absent. The revision is targeted to exclusivity and resolves the original conflict with Section 12.3. The operative text, rather than the margin comment, supports the result.
